subject: Hosted evaluation: deployment decision checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finso.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Sep 2029 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up on today's demo — deployment fit questions

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo earlier — it was helpful to see the runtime behavior on our sample prompts. Priya and I discussed internally and we want to sharpen requirements so we can pick a deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). A few immediate questions so we can scope the pilot: 

- Peak qps: we expect spikes up to ~80 QPS for short windows (~10-15 min), baseline ~6–10 QPS. Can hosted support burst capacity that high without a multi-week provisioning step?
- Latency SLO: target p95 <= 250ms for short responses (<= 120 tokens). Is that realistic on hosted for the open model you suggested?
- Data residency: some transactions must stay in US regions (no EU egress). Can hosted endpoints be region-pinned?
- Security: we will need SOC2 evidence and a short answers sheet on data retention and KV cache persistence.

Also — we have a small subset of sensitive prompts we'd like to test in a private VPC if hosted can't meet the residency or latency needs. What's your recommendation for a first pilot (sandbox endpoints, rate limits, and timeline)?

If you can send a short checklist/next-steps we can route to procurement and engineering.

Best,
Liam
Product @ FinSo

Hi Liam, Priya —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers first, then proposed next steps below. Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if you want to run through the traffic CSV together.

1) Burst capacity: Hosted can absorb short spikes via burst capacity and autoscaling for most open-model workloads. For sustained 80 QPS we recommend either a short reserved Dedicated window or enabling burst policy (we can provision a burst pool within 3 business days for trials).

2) Latency p95: For concise responses (<=120 tokens) p95 <= 250ms is achievable on hosted for the 7B–13B class models with our endpoint routing and KV prefix cache enabled. We'll need your exact prompt length distribution (the CSV helps) and whether you need streaming.

3) Region pinning: Yes — hosted endpoints can be pinned to a US region and we can restrict routing to that region for the pilot.

4) Security evidence: attaching the quickstart playbook with a SOC2 summary and data retention notes. For KV cache, we treat caches as ephemeral unless you opt into customer-managed persistence in Private deployments.

Suggested pilot plan (minimal friction):
- Step A (this week): Redwood provides a sandbox Hosted endpoint (US) with a 30k-token/day budget, a burst buffer (up to 100 QPS for 10 minutes) and conservative rate limits mapped to your CSV.
- Step B (week 2): Measure p95 on your test prompts; enable prefix KV caching to validate latency improvements.
- Step C (week 3): If sustained high QPS is required, convert to a short Dedicated reservation or evaluate Private VPC for strict egress/residency.

Action items for FinSo (please):
- Confirm which US region you'd like pinned (us-west-2 or us-east-1).
- Share a redacted set of 200 test prompts (can be a subset of your CSV).
- Confirm whether streaming is required for the pilot.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-playbook.pdf, deployment-matrix.xlsx

I'll loop Marissa for pricing and the standard trial contract; Karthik will help with endpoint config and rate mappings.

Thanks —
Ava
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Sep 2029 07:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted evaluation: deployment decision checklist & next steps

Ava / Marissa — technical confirmation and suggested defaults below.

- Endpoint config: single US-west-2 sandbox endpoint, model variant: rw-open-13B-std (quantized CPU/GPU mix)
- Rate limits: baseline 10 RPS, burst buffer up to 100 RPS for 15 minutes (token-based throttling enabled)
- Concurrency ceiling: 90 concurrent streams; keep worker count flexible during trial
- KV cache: enable prefix caching with TTL 300s; caches are local to runtime (ephemeral) on Hosted — recommend cache warmup script during load test
- Metrics: enable per-request tracing and latency histograms; we'll provide a dashboard with p50/p95/p99 and token-cost breakdown

Notes: If FinSo requires strict persistence for KV or customer-managed keys, we should recommend Private VPC. For residency, routing is enforced at the control plane level to ensure US-only egress.

I'll prepare an endpoint config snippet and a short runbook for the customer test steps.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
